convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load the 'Oracle' custom indicator which is not a built-in MT5 indicator. Also depends on TradeAlgorithms.mqh external library for position open/close logic, money management, and new bar detection.

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars required for calculation
TimeShiftSec - chart period in seconds
derived_values.used_by: UpSignalTime/DnSignalTime calculation for position open calls

other_exits: BuyPosClose/SellPosClose called when opposite signal detected, controlled by BuyPosClose/SellPosClose input flags

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM input: negative values = fixed lot size (e.g. -0.1 means 0.1 lots), positive values = share of deposit in a deal (fractional sizing)

custom_logic_notes: Three entry algorithms selectable via Mode enum: 1) 'breakdown' - signal line crosses zero; 2) 'twist' - signal line changes direction (compares 3 consecutive bars); 3) 'disposition' - signal line crosses main indicator line. SignalBar parameter controls which bar index is used for signal detection (default=1 means previous completed bar). Recount flag ensures signals are recalculated on first tick or when CopyBuffer fails. LoadHistory ensures historical data is available for IsNewBar and SeriesInfoInteger. Position open/close functions are from TradeAlgorithms.mqh library which likely handles position checking, margin validation, and order execution internally.
python_conversion_notes: The Oracle custom indicator is not available in Python - its formula must be obtained from the Oracle.mq5 indicator source code and reimplemented. TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, CIsNewBar, LoadHistory, GlobalVariableDel_) must be reimplemented. The MM parameter has dual meaning: negative=lot size, positive=deposit fraction - this conditional sizing logic must be preserved. The three entry modes (breakdown, twist, disposition) each have different signal detection logic using different buffer combinations and bar counts from the Oracle indicator.
